title: Show the Neumann ceiling U is below 10 p^2 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For every integer `p ≥ 2`, the within-cell Neumann ceiling

```text
U = 8 p^2 (D - 4) / (D - 32 p^2),    D = 2^{32760 p},
```

satisfies `U < 10 p^2`. The coefficient 8 does not: `U > 8 p^2` exactly when `32 p^2 > 4`.

This is a property of the formula. It is an inverse bound only when the #4452 gauge holds. In that case the Neumann 1-norm and ∞-norm are already strictly below `U`, hence strictly below `10 p^2`. The ideal gaps stay hypotheses. No new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

This answers the open question of #4491. It does not replay #4452. The smallest integer coefficient is left open.

## Comparison

With a positive denominator, `U < 10 p^2` is equivalent to `8(D - 4) < 10(D - 32 p^2)`. The difference is

```text
10(D - 32 p^2) - 8(D - 4) = 2(D - 160 p^2 + 16).
```

So it is enough that `D > 160 p^2 - 16`. For `p ≥ 2`, `2^{2p} ≥ p^2 + 1`, hence `160 p^2 < 2^{2p+8}`. The exponent gap `32760 p - (2p + 8) = 32758 p - 8` is 65508 at `p = 2` and increases, so `2^{2p+8} < D`. The same estimate gives `D > 32 p^2`.
